title: Great House Farm: research questions
note: Same item shape as /qa/kb.json (kind: case). Sources were read on 13 and 14 November 2026. Open points stay open until a second source settles them.

items.question: Which other recorded buildings stood within 200 m of the house, and do site files survive for them?
items.answer:
The national record (Coflein) has four entries close to the house besides Great House Farm itself (NPRN 20182). NPRN 15342 is "Llandough, Remains of House At", a medieval house at ST 1682 7320, about 110 m south of the house. NPRN 19886 is Rose Cottage, a later 17th-century house at ST 1674 7320, ruinous when surveyed in 1964 and since demolished, about 130 m to the south-west. NPRN 19159 is Llandough Grange, a post-medieval dwelling at ST 1685 7313, about 185 m to the south-south-east. NPRN 400051 is the Roman villa site at ST 1680 7330, excavated in 1979. The entries for 15342 and 19159 carry no description. Distances are worked from the grid references, which are given to 10 m.

Points for:
• Coflein NPRN 15342, 19159, 19886 and 400051 (read 13 November 2026)

Not yet established:
• Whether NPRN 15342 is the same medieval house remains reported south of the church in 1963 and 1979
• Which of these stood on the house parcel, the fields parcel or neither

Records still to check:
• The National Monuments Record site files behind NPRN 15342, 19159 and 19886 (an enquiry is drafted, not sent)
• The tithe map and apportionment, for the plot numbers under each grid reference

items.question: What do the Mathew family papers show about Llandough and Leckwith holdings before the Bute estate?
items.answer:
Glamorgan Archives holds the papers of the Mathew family of Radyr and Llandaff (DMAT). The published list runs to DMAT 206–207. It records a Vaughan holding in the manor of Leckwith in 1682, other owners granting land there in 1715, 1729 and 1734, and Mathews "of Llandough" through the 18th century. A later item, DMAT/279, is a late 18th-century plan of "Ty Mawr farm, Llandough [Gedrych property]" (photocopy; catalogue record MED-0208).

Points for:
• DMAT 168: surrender and admission of Morris Vaughan to a tenement and land in the manor of Leckwith, November 1682
• DMAT 177: Thomas, Viscount Windsor, conveys a cottage and land in the manor of Leckwith to Lewis Morgan of Leckwith, yeoman, 7 and 8 December 1715
• DMAT 170 and 171: a cottage and land near Leckwith church, leased by the Dowager Countess of Pembroke on 23 October 1729; a 99-year lease at the Manor of Leckwith Court and Audit, 5 December 1734
• DMAT 2, 7, 60, 187 and 189: Anthony Mathew of Llandough (will, 1740), William Mathew of Llandough (leases, 1770 and 1774), William John of Llandough, farmer (marriage bond, 1774), John Mathew of Llandough (inventory, 1805)
• DMAT 69: copy entries from the Leckwith, Llandough and Michaelston-le-Pit parish registers
• DMAT 175–176: William Gedrych of Leckwith, with Leckwith Farm in his occupation, 1829; DMAT 53: Gedrych v. Mathew, 1829

Not yet established:
• Which Llandough the Mathew entries mean. DMAT 69 groups Llandough with Leckwith and Michaelston-le-Pit, which points to Llandough near Penarth; the list does not state it
• Whether Morris Vaughan of 1682 belongs to the Vaughan family recorded at Great House
• Which land the "Gedrych property" plan covers, and where the original plan is held

A name to keep apart: "Great House" in these papers is usually the Mathew family's house at Whitchurch, a different place.

Records still to check:
• The list for DMAT 208 onwards, and the catalogue entry for DMAT/279 (an enquiry is drafted, not sent)
• DMAT 168, 171 and 177 themselves

sources.label: Glamorgan Archives DMAT list (The National Archives, Discovery)

items.question: Do the Plymouth (Windsor) estate plans show the boundary with the Great House holding?
items.answer:
Three plans in the Plymouth estate collection at Glamorgan Archives (DPL) cover Llandough before and at the time of the tithe survey. None has been seen yet. A plan of a neighbouring estate marks its own edge, so these may show where the Windsor and Clive lands stopped and who held the land next to them.

Points for:
• DPL/6: plan of Lord Plymouth's estates in Penarth, Llandough, Cogan and Lavernock, about 1768
• DPL/7: rough sketch maps, about 1820–1840, including a tracing for Llandough
• DPL/8: plan of Lady H. Clive's lands in Cogan and Llandough parishes, about 1840

Not yet established:
• Whether any of the three reaches the land beside St Dochdwy's Church
• Whether the neighbouring owners and occupiers are named on them

Records still to check:
• DPL/6, DPL/7 and DPL/8 (an enquiry on copying is drafted, not sent)
• The Plymouth rentals and abstract of leases for Glamorgan, 1712–1797, in the same collection

sources.label: Glamorgan Archives DPL list (The National Archives, Discovery)

items.question: What has Welsh Government published about the 1988 Cadw inspection?
items.answer:
Welsh Government published its response to request ATISN 27021 on its disclosure log, dated 11 June 2026. It records that Cadw inspectors visited and assessed the house and that it did not meet the criteria for listing. The only record it holds is two inspection photographs, of the house and of the barn, dated 29 July 1988. It holds nothing else for 1970–1999, and records that other papers would have gone to the Royal Commission (RCAHMW) or been destroyed under the Public Records Act 1958.

Points for:
• Welsh Government disclosure log, ATISN 27021, 11 June 2026

Not yet established:
• The inspectors' written assessment, and the date and authority for the disposal of the 1988 file

Records still to check:
• RCAHMW, for anything received from Cadw or the Welsh Office in 1988–89
• The replies to ATISN 26-0009 and 26-0075, listed in the hall

items.question: What did the Ministry of Defence state about armed forces involvement in 1988?
items.answer:
The Ministry of Defence replied to request FOI2026/09019 on 29 May 2026, and the reply is published on WhatDoTheyKnow. For Special Forces it relied on section 23(5) of the Freedom of Information Act and would neither confirm nor deny that information is held, adding that this is no indication either way. For the rest of the request (military aid to the civil authorities, and correspondence with the police, the council and the Welsh Office) it stated that no information is held. It pointed to The National Archives at Kew for unit historical records and commanders' diaries of the period.

Points for:
• Ministry of Defence reply, FOI2026/09019, 29 May 2026

Not yet established:
• Which record systems and date ranges were searched for the part reported as not held

Records still to check:
• The National Archives: unit historical records and commanders' diaries for late 1988
• The internal review of FOI2026/09019, listed in the hall

items.question: Where did Marconi stay during the May 1897 trials, and who was the Mr Williams at Lavernock?
items.answer:
The family account is that Marconi lodged at Great House during the trials and that a Mr Williams of the house helped with a horse and cart. No record made at the time and naming the house has been found yet. A 1993 journal article puts Marconi's headquarters for the trials at the Penarth Hotel, with the trials at Lavernock Point between 6 and 29 May 1897. The Evening Express of 15 May 1897, as transcribed in a 2019 local history article, names "Mr Williams (of the engineering department, Cardiff)" as fixing a 120-foot pole at Lavernock Point. That is a second Williams at the trials, so the two must not be merged.

Points for:
• The family account, repeated in the 1974 press reports

Points against:
• BIAS Journal 26 (1993): headquarters at the Penarth Hotel
• Post Office Limited, FOI2026/00751: no record held of a Mr Williams and the 1897 experiments

Not yet established:
• Where Marconi's assistants and the Post Office staff lodged
• Whether the Mr Williams of the newspaper report was a Post Office engineer with no link to the house

Records still to check:
• The Evening Express page of 15 May 1897 itself (Welsh Newspapers Online)
• George Kemp's diaries for May 1897 (Marconi Archives, Bodleian Library)
